title: Captain Mandible
subtitle: Falmouth for Orders
description: A box comes down out of an aunt's roof, soft with damp, and inside the newspaper and a tea towel there is a skull. Every family has an indiscretion it keeps upstairs. Nobody has seen this one. Everybody can tell you which room it wasn't allowed in. He is a Mandeville, four generations back, a master under sail, and he has not finished talking.
tagline: Everybody knows which room it isn’t allowed in.
blurb: The box comes down out of the roof at Hessie's, the cardboard gone soft as a wet digestive. Newspaper inside, a good nest of it, then a folded tea towel with a Dutch windmill on it, and inside the tea towel, him.
Nobody tells you the weight.

He is a Mandeville, four generations back, a master under sail, and he has not finished talking. He has opinions about the nose he no longer has, about the century he has woken into, and about the schoolteacher now holding him under a good lamp at the kitchen table.

Falmouth for orders: a grain ship left Australia and sailed three months without knowing where she was bound, because the market moved faster than she did. She came up the Channel, anchored, and waited for a telegram to tell her where she was going.

title: The Petrosphere Odyssey
subtitle: An Ancient Pilgrimage
description: A young woman at the end of her rope comes into the keeping of a small dark stone. Guided by a grandmother's journal, she walks an old road through the north of Scotland, and nine recognitions slowly put her back together.

title: The Honest Pilgrim
subtitle: The Journey of Impossible Answers
description: Every answer runs out. This book begins where they stop. A boy collects questions the way other children collect stones, and he has noticed something no adult will admit: their answers run out, usually three questions deep. Then his grandfather dies in the middle of a sentence, and the boy takes down an old hand-drawn map and asks for the road. Fifteen Steps lie between his gate and the small mark at the end of the longest road. A fable meant to be taken slowly: one Step a night, then twenty minutes outside with nothing in your hands.

title: Coherence
subtitle: The Essence and The Form
description: There are plenty of books about reaching that moment. There are very few about the morning after it. Fifty-two short stories that are really twenty-six, each one told twice. In The Essence, a recognition is compressed into a single held image. In The Form, the same recognition is lived by a particular person, in a particular week, at what it actually cost. The people are ordinary and the weather is northern. There is nothing to join, nothing to believe, and nothing at the end to buy.

title: Welcome Home
subtitle: The Medicine Letters
description: Forty-five human aches, each named in the words you might use yourself. “I am tired of being the strong one.” “No one has ever really known me.” “I am coming home.” Each ache is met by a small chorus of letters: the first from the field, the rest from ten guides who know the territory from the inside. They do not explain your pain, and they do not try to fix you. They sit down beside you and ask for nothing. Read slowly. Skip freely. Return when it hurts.

title: It's Only a Walk
subtitle: Nine things Cyprus never wrote down
description: A dead woman's house. A hand-drawn map. Nine points, none of them labelled. And on the back, in black biro, four words: Walk it or don't. Andreas Loizou has ten days set aside to sell an aunt's house on Cyprus. He stays nine months, because the map in her kitchen drawer is real, and its nine points lead him across a divided island to the nine things it has never written down. Not mysticism: nine usable insights about attention, worry, and the worlds we build without noticing.
blurb: There are nine things that can be understood on this island and nowhere else, and they have never been written down.

Andreas Loizou comes to Cyprus to sell a house he never lived in, left by an aunt he barely knew. In her kitchen drawer he finds a map of the island, traced by hand in biro, with nine unmarked points and four words on the back: Walk it or don't.

Guided by a retired schoolteacher who refuses to explain anything, he walks it, October to the summer solstice: a street with a border across it, a sealed city, a church full of eyes, a mountain that listens to the whole sea and can do nothing. At every point, something the island learned the hard way, over eight hundred years, about how people hold together when nothing else does.
And every month, on a headland that moves, there is a party. The sun touches the sea. It takes four minutes. Nobody owns it, nobody can sell it, and it asks you to believe nothing at all.
The walk has no finish line. It has a chair.

title: Beyond the Pale
subtitle: Where Giants Sleep, book one
description: Robyn is seventeen, furious, and four hundred miles from everything she knows. Her mother is a year dead; her father has moved them to a school at the edge of Scotland and a house with a locked hangar at the bottom of the garden; and the only thing that still makes sense is the weight of a foil in her hand.
tagline: Some borders are places. This one is a moment.
blurb: Robyn is seventeen, furious, and four hundred miles from everything she knows. Her mother is a year dead; her father has moved them to a school at the edge of Scotland and a house with a locked hangar at the bottom of the garden; and the only thing that still makes sense is the weight of a foil in her hand.
Then she learns what her father keeps in the hangar. And why, in 1978, four boys walked out of this school and never walked back.

Beyond the pale there is a country where your life is worth exactly what you carry in glass, where the weather hunts, and where the one rule that matters is her father’s: note the exact time you arrived.
Robyn thinks the strangest thing about the Cage is that she can cross into it at all. She is wrong. The strangest thing is how well it knows her.

title: Pauper's Weatherglass
subtitle: Where Giants Sleep, book two
description: Robyn came home with a story she can never tell, and marbles she should not have. She has a degree now, a life, a best friend who asks no questions. It has almost been enough.
tagline: The flower closes before the rain.
blurb: Robyn came home with a story she can never tell, and marbles she should not have. She has a degree now, a life, a best friend who asks no questions. It has almost been enough.
Then, in the crowd at her graduation, she sees a man who cannot possibly be there.

The Cage wants her back, and this time it will not take a schoolgirl. It takes a Baroness with borrowed papers, a smuggler’s ship with a wrong name, a resistance that trades in the one currency that matters, and a man called Lord London who keeps other people’s treasures because they are safer with him. Robyn will lie her way to the top of a world to finish what the missing boys began, and she will discover what it costs to hold on to what you win.
And under everything, faint as a fridge in another room, there is a sound she has learned not to hear. One note. Steady. Counting.

title: The Persistence of Memory
subtitle: Where Giants Sleep, book three
description: Five years have passed since the Cage let Robyn go, and life at the bottom of the garden is kind. Her son is growing. The house is warm. The light is always exactly where she needs it.
blurb: Five years have passed since the Cage let Robyn go, and life at the bottom of the garden is kind. Her son is growing. The house is warm. The light is always exactly where she needs it.
That is the problem.

Because lately there are flashes: a rail cold under her hand, a tube low in her throat, a voice a hand’s breadth away saying her name into a dark it is not sure can hear. And once Robyn pulls the first loose thread, the whole warm world begins to come apart in her lap.

Somewhere above her there is a room. In the room there is a woman who has never once stopped saying it: to the moon and back. Twelve marbles will get Robyn there. She has six. And the world is draining while she counts.
